P7s1: The Zapatistas are also the closest whole example that I found, because their autonomy goes beyond how they vote. They've set up their own education and health care, and their own justice, and they've built their own collective production and political formation. On top of that they've worked out ways of teaching outsiders. They do all of this while coordinating beyond a single village.

And they do all of this while coordinating beyond a single village.
P13o1: Now, the Zapatistas also don't prove my whole economic path, from unpriced internal necessities, to a common purse, to getting rid of outside money. Do their communities use collective work to support their schools and clinics, and their autonomous government and resistance? Yes. But they also sell products and trade, and they get outside support. So what do they show? That major necessities and public functions can come out of ordinary market purchase and be governed collectively instead. Outside help can make a community more capable, sure. But if the specialist or the donor or the organization stays indispensable, that help can also create gatekeepers and uneven dependence.

P15g1: One way an escuelita could fail is if it becomes a business, where residents spend their lives performing community for paying outsiders, and success gets measured by how many people come instead of how many daughter communities there are. A week of feeling transformed isn't what it's for. It's for teaching enough of the social and material system that some people can build somewhere else.

Giving people a week where they feel transformed isn't what it's for. It's for teaching enough of the social and material system that some of them can go build somewhere else.
P4h: Oventik itself was like something out of a dream. We played basketball on an outdoor court with the Zapatista youth, and people gave us talks about their history and philosophy, and I translated for my friends because my Spanish was better. Visitors were coming from all around the world to learn, and to make the communities less easy to attack in silence.
